A non-conference clash shines under the lights when the Chicago Bears host the New England Patriots for Thursday Night Football. Chicago welcomed star quarterback Caleb Williams back from injury this weekend, and his presence has the home team laying just short of a field goal against the defending AFC champs. My Bears vs. Patriots predictions size up the opening action and current forms, giving my early leans and NFL picks for TNF on Oct. 22. Patriots vs Bears predictions For help understanding Kalshi probabilities, see our odds calculator . Percentages courtesy of Kalshi , one of the best prediction market apps . Early Patriots vs Bears spread pick: Bears -2.5 The Chicago Bears and New England Patriots were both victorious in Week 6, but neither looked like world beaters. Chicago benefited from multiple blunders by Atlanta and still had to sweat it out in the fourth quarter. New England escaped the Jets but didn't cover at home, thanks to New York stubbing its toe on crucial fourth downs. Prime-time pups have been the trendy play over the past few weeks, but I'm not convinced the Patriots can compete in the Bears' weight class, at least on offense. All eyes are on RB2 Kyle Monangai, who has missed time with turf toe. Chicago's ground game is underrated and can get after a Pats run defense that's been pushed around. Monangai's return would give the Bears a boost. I'll lean toward the home side at anything short of the key number of three. Start trading with Kalshi today! As dangerous as this Chicago offense can be, the Bears' stop unit is just as sharp. Chicago recorded five sacks on Atlanta in Week 6, and its blitz-centric pass rush is drumming up a high rate of pressure and creating opportunities for game-changing plays, like INTs and sacks. The New England offensive line is a mess right now, with multiple starters missing. The short week doesn't do quarterback Drake Maye any favors in that regard. Maye has cleaned up his mistakes from early in the season but has faced some softer, less dangerous defenses over the past three games. I'm going to lean Under the taller total, given that the Bears can grind out gains on the ground and force Maye into some miscues. Fresh off the win at Atlanta, the Bears come home to host last year's Super Bowl runner-up at Soldier Field and are currently 3-point favorites. It's generally understood in gambling that home-field advantage is worth 3 points, so the oddsmakers think the two teams are pretty evenly matched. The Patriots beat the Jets in Foxboro today 26-19. picks.blurb: Thursday Night Football Preview: Patriots and Bears Set for Primetime Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Thunder stifle Wemby, Spurs World Series preview 76ers beat Knicks War of words over Hurts NFL Power Rankings Thursday Night Football Preview: Patriots and Bears Set for Primetime Showdown Photo by: Brett Davis Stephan Stroud Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:52 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads New England and Chicago Battle for Momentum in Week 7 Thursday Night Football brings an exciting matchup to Soldier Field as the New England Patriots visit the Chicago Bears on October 22. Both teams enter the Week 7 contest with identical 4-2 records, making this an important opportunity for two teams looking to strengthen their position in the playoff race. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. With both teams coming off victories, fans should expect a competitive matchup between two offenses that have shown plenty of potential this season. Drake Maye Looks to Continue His Hot Streak The Patriots enter Thursday's game riding a three-game winning streak, and quarterback Drake Maye has been a major reason for their recent success. New England has defeated the Buffalo Bills, Las Vegas Raiders and New York Jets during its current run. The Patriots' 47-17 victory over Las Vegas highlighted their offensive potential, while Sunday's 26-19 win against the Jets showed their ability to compete in a tighter game. Maye has looked increasingly comfortable leading the offense under head coach Mike Vrabel. His ability to make accurate throws, extend plays and distribute the football to his playmakers will be important against Chicago's defense. However, New England has some concerns entering the matchup. Injuries along the offensive line could make it difficult to protect Maye, particularly against a Bears defense looking to create pressure. Wide receiver A.J. Brown is also dealing with an ankle injury, making his availability an important storyline heading into Thursday night. Caleb Williams Leads a Dangerous Bears Offense Chicago also enters the game with plenty of confidence after defeating the Atlanta Falcons 31-23 on Sunday Night Football. Quarterback Caleb Williams returned to the lineup and delivered an impressive performance, throwing for 305 yards while helping Chicago control the game offensively. Williams has the arm talent and playmaking ability to challenge opposing defenses, and his return provides a significant boost to the Bears. Running backs D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson also give Chicago options on the ground, helping create balance and prevent defenses from focusing entirely on the passing game. Head coach Ben Johnson will look to keep the offense aggressive while taking advantage of New England's injury concerns. Key Matchups to Watch The battle in the trenches could determine how this game unfolds. If New England protects Maye, the Patriots have the offensive weapons to challenge Chicago throughout the night. Meanwhile, the Bears will look to establish their running game and give Williams opportunities to attack downfield. Turnovers will also be crucial. Both teams have demonstrated the ability to score, meaning one costly mistake could shift momentum in a hurry. A Major Test for Both Teams With both teams sitting at 4-2, Thursday night's matchup carries plenty of importance. New England wants to extend its winning streak, while Chicago hopes to build on Williams' successful return. The Patriots and Bears have each shown they can compete, but this primetime showdown will provide another opportunity to demonstrate their progress as the NFL season moves toward its midpoint.

picks.headline: Saints' Moore Speaks From Paris: Giants Win, Injuries and Steelers Preview
picks.blurb: Saints' Moore Speaks From Paris: Giants Win, Injuries and Steelers Preview Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints have arrived in Paris, France, with much-needed momentum after Sunday's 34-27 victory over the New York Giants . Fresh off ending a three-game skid, the Saints face the Pittsburgh Steelers in an international matchup that requires adjusting to a seven-hour time zone difference. Head coach Kellen Moore noted Monday that arriving early gives players time to acclimate before Wednesday's practices and offers a team-bonding opportunity following their game in New Jersey. Reflecting on the win over New York, Moore praised the rushing attack, takeaways, and mid-game execution, but stressed the need to finish better after nearly losing a 34-10 fourth-quarter lead. He also addressed rookie Jeremiah Wright's performance, injuries, and his history with Steelers coach Mike McCarthy from their time in Dallas. Here is what Moore had to say about the Saints' arrival in Paris, Sunday's victory and preparations for Pittsburgh. Full Transcript from Monday’s Presser Opening Statement Bonjour. We're here. We just got here. Good travel, all that. Our guys were able to get out on the field and walk around and get a light lift in at the hotel. Obviously, there's a little bit of an acclimation process, but I think it's a great setup. It's an awesome opportunity for our football team to spend some time together while focusing on a really good opportunity to play out here in a great atmosphere. It's been a really fun week. Q: Why was it important for the team to arrive in Paris early? I think there's a few elements. The acclimation thing is important. For our guys to get here, have a couple days to get acclimated, and then it allows us to have a normal workflow. Wednesday through Sunday is going to be as normal as possible. I think that's going to be a great opportunity for our guys. There's always an added bonus of guys having an opportunity to spend a little bit more time together. The bonding element of a team atmosphere, I think it'll be great for our guys. This is obviously a continuation of an extended trip going from New York to here. I think this will be great. Q: Will you have to make any adjustments to team activities because of the events and protests taking place in Paris? There's not really anything organized from a team bonding standpoint. I think it's more our guys having the opportunity to spend some time together, and that'll naturally, organically occur. I think guys will have different opportunities to share a meal or spend a little bit of time outside. That's at their discretion. Our guys are smart. They understand this is still a business trip. At the same time, there'll be a little bit of time for these guys to explore. I think that's an important part of this thing. Go explore. You're in a different country, a different culture. It's a great opportunity. Then we have a normal week, just like we always do. Q: How has the seven-hour time difference affected your process of reviewing Sunday's game, both for the coaching staff and the players? We'll go through our process as similarly as possible. Obviously, we haven't gotten through all that yet. Essentially, it was game, back to the hotel in New York — in New Jersey, technically — and then we flew out. We just got here. We went through the acclimation process a little bit. We'll start getting into some meetings and some film to review the game and get ourselves moving forward toward Pittsburgh. Q: Do you feel a little lighter or relieved after Sunday's victory? I'm just proud of our guys. NFL seasons always take their different courses, and there's emotions related to every game. Everyone has the same goals and aspirations. I thought our guys obviously did enough to win that football game, so credit to them. I thought that middle eight was a critical part of that game. It put us in position. Obviously, we know there's going to be opportunities to focus on some things we need to improve on, certainly the finish. Ultimately, we got it done, but we want to finish better. I thought our guys were really resilient and stuck together. I thought there was juice and energy, and I love that. I love the turnovers on defense. I love running the football on offense. I love the kickoff team creating another turnover. That unit's been special. I thought there were some big plays throughout that game. Q: Do you have an injury update on Cesar (Ruiz), and did Kaden (Ellis) and Jordyn (Tyson) make the trip? They're on the trip, and I do not have a detailed medical update yet. Q: Was it difficult managing the injured players during a long flight immediately after Sunday's game? The medical evaluations coming out of the game, you obviously have more time to go through that process. We had to get a few guys through the evaluation phase, and then obviously the travel. I think this is an important part, getting out here. It's not a perfect setup with the travel and all that sort of stuff. But for us to be able to do it coming right out of the game, get here, now our guys get to get acclimated. They'll get adjusted to this time zone pretty well. We'll get the different place, tourist thing out of our system here quickly and then get into a full week. Q: What contributed to the improvement in the running game against the Giants? I think all 11. At the end of the day, it was all 11. Physical up front. I thought our running backs ran really, really hard. Receivers getting into the safeties and some of those things, and tight ends battling. I thought we had a good mix there. We've got to continue that. We've got to build on that. I thought some of our combination blocks, when we were able to get those going, were very effective. Q: What did you think of rookie offensive lineman Jeremiah Wright's performance in his first extended playing opportunity? I thought he did some good things. First time really playing an extended period of time. Proud of him for stepping up and taking advantage of the opportunity. I thought that was a good first start for him as far as getting out there and playing some football. We know these seasons, guys have to hop in there and take advantage of an opportunity and continue to get better. Jeremiah was able to step in there, and that's what you need in this league. You're going to need guys to be called upon, and you never know when your opportunity is going to present itself. You've got to take advantage of it. Good job by him. Q: Was the middle eight against the Giants the best stretch of complementary football your team has played this season? Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. We've had moments, and certainly that's what the NFL is. There's highs and lows in every season, every game. That's just how it is. We want to play more consistent football. We've got to get there. I thought that was a big deal. I thought our defense had some stops in there to control the game, got that long field goal, and then the kickoff unit creating that turnover was special. We were able to score right before half, and then the third quarter, I felt like we came out playing the way we needed to play. Q: What do you like about the team's practice facility in Paris, and will the Saints have an opportunity to visit the stadium before Sunday? The whole organization and the league have done a phenomenal job of getting ahead of this thing, putting us in a really good setup from a proximity standpoint of the hotel and the training facility and where we'll be able to practice. I feel like it's going to be a great setup for us. We already went over there for a little walk. Our guys got some fresh air and walked around the field to see where it's at. We'll go to the stadium Saturday so our guys can see it and experience that a little bit, so Sunday's not the first time. It'll be a great opportunity. This is going to be a great environment for us. I think this is really well set up. Appreciate everything our organization's done, Mrs. B's done, to help set this thing up for us to have a great week. Q: What does facing Mike McCarthy mean to you, considering your previous coaching relationship with him? Obviously, both of our staffs have a healthy dose of carryover. We have a lot of ties. Mike was awesome for me. Being a younger coach, I was a first-time offensive coordinator, then he came to Dallas, and I was able to stay on and learn so much from him. He's a great family man. I appreciate the way he operated. It'll be great to see him and great to see a number of the guys over there on that staff who I've spent a number of years with. Q: How many croissants have you eaten since arriving in Paris? It'll probably happen fast here. All I see is Doug in his little cafe over there. That's all I'm seeing on my screen this entire time. Doug's already rolling. He's going all in. I think he's already had a croissant today, too. Published Oct 20, 2026 GRANT CHACHERE A New Orleans native, Grant covers the New Orleans Saints for On SI. He returned to the Big Easy after serving as the lead beat reporter for North Carolina Tar Heels On SI. After graduating from LSU in 2023, he covered the local prep sports scene for Crescent City Sports and wrote columns on the Saints on the site as well. He began his sports reporting career with WGNO in 2022, serving as a stringer for its award-winning high school football show, Friday Night Lights, while attending LSU. When he is not writing about the Black and Gold, he also contributes LSU coverage to TigerBait and FanSided’s Death Valley Voice. picks.blurb: Week 7 odds: Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Thunder stifle Wemby, Spurs World Series preview 76ers beat Knicks War of words over Hurts NFL Power Rankings Week 7 odds: Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Saints (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jason Aponte Tue, October 20, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a tough road win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as three-point favorites despite the neutral site. The Saints are coming off a victory of their own after a furious comeback attempt by the New York Giants, and J.J. McCarthy fell just short. The over/under is 44.5, and Steelers moneyline odds sit at -174. The line will move with injury news from both teams, but this feels right. On the one hand, the Saints offense is a handful, but the defense, aside from Chase Young and a few other players, is vulnerable. The key will be getting off to a faster start on offense and defense. At the beginning of the Tampa Bay game and for much of the game, the Steelers felt stuck in neutral. The offense and defense kicked it into gear down the stretch and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard was fantastic and has quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers. Trust me, that isn't easy to earn. Rodgers and Bernard looked like Rodgers and Cobb from the Packers days. D.K. Metcalf turned in a big game and made critical plays down the stretch. While the receiver room gets healthy, the two receivers will need to continue making plays. Jaylen Warren slowed down off his torrid pace, but Rico Dowdle was effective on Sunday. Still, at the end of the game, Warren was the one making big plays in overtime. It's the NFL and every game is difficult, but the Steelers need this one and Vegas believes they will get it done. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let's take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus © Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh's lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh's defense will give him room to correct it. New Orleans' opponents have averaged 256.0 passing yards per game, which suggests quarterbacks can find openings in this matchup. Rookie Germie Bernard's 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers' last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Pittsburgh, but turnovers and a motivated passing offense can make this matchup less predictable than the records suggest. NFL Betting Odds, Point Spread, Trends There is a lot of civil unrest happening in France right now, but the game will go on as scheduled – at least for now. The Saints already are over there as they flew out directly from the New York area after playing there Sunday. The Steelers will to practice in Pittsburgh before departing for France on Thursday. Of course, Louisiana was once a French territory, so it made all the sense in the world for New Orleans to be the first team to “host” a game over there. This will mark the final international game in the Hall of Fame career of Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who has said he will retire after this season (and seems to mean it). He obviously will be a big draw to the local fans as one of the league's biggest stars the past two decades or so. Rodgers led the Steelers to a win in the NFL's first game in Ireland last year against Minnesota. These franchises have met 17 times, all in the regular season, and the Saints lead 9-8. The last met in 2022, and the Steelers prevailed 20-10 at home to end a three-game skid in the series. NFL Player Odds and Props Bet Pittsburgh's Aaron Rodgers for at least two TD passes as he has found the Fountain of Youth of sorts with at least two in four straight games. Pittsburgh is in a three-way tie for first in the AFC North after a 26-19 overtime comeback win in Tampa on Sunday – the Bucs were up 16-3 in the third quarter. But Aaron Rodgers had a fourth-quarter TD pass and the winning TD throw in overtime. In doing so, he tied fellow legend and multiple-time MVP Peyton Manning for third on the NFL's career list with 539 career TD throws. Only Tom Brady (649) and Drew Brees (571) have more. It was Rodgers' 14 th career comeback win of at least 13 points, third-most by any QB since 1950. It snapped his personal 31-game losing streak when trailing by more than 10 points in a game, which was the NFL's longest active by a QB. Rodgers, playing without injured receivers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson, hit Germie Bernard on that winning TD, and Bernard became the first rookie in league annals with at least 10 receptions and an overtime touchdown in a game. The Steelers had been undefeated at home but 0-2 on the road. The Saints are really hard to figure out. They looked so good in a Week 2 upset in Baltimore, then so badly in a three-game home losing streak. Only to look good again Sunday and save the season with a 34-27 victory at the New York Giants. New Orleans has now trailed by double digits in both victories, and it outrushed New York 175-84. It scored 34 consecutive points after down 10-0. The Saints entered allowing 148.8 rush yards per game, among the worst in the league. Second-year QB Tyler Shough had his first career game with at least three TD passes and no picks. It was already his fourth career win when trailing in a game by double digits, fourth-most by any Saints signal-caller. He is playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand. New Orleans played without a starting defender up front and at linebacker and then saw secondary players Kool-Aid McKinstry and Quincy Riley leave injured. Getty Dave Holcomb Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:07 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling has found a new home — again. On Monday, he landed in one of his former homes with a very familiar quarterback. The Athletic's Mike DeFabo reported Monday night the Pittsburgh Steelers plan to sign Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad. The deal will reunite the veteran wideout with quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who he has previously played with in five other seasons. Last year, Valdes-Scantling also joined the Steelers near the midseason point. He caught 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown from Rodgers. From 2018-21, he played with the future Hall of Fame quarterback with the Green Bay Packers. This offseason, Valdes-Scantling signed a 1-year, $1.49 million contract with the Cowboys. But Dallas released the veteran at the NFL roster deadline at the end of August. In mid-season, Valdes-Scantling joined the Los Angeles Chargers . The Chargers released the receiver over the weekend. Ex-Cowboys WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling Rejoins Aaron Rodgers GettyFormer Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling is expected to join the Pittsburgh Steelers practice squad. The Steelers will be adding Valdes-Scantling for much needed depth. Pittsburgh has suffered three injuries at receiver over the past three weeks. Only two wideouts caught a pass from Rodgers on Sunday despite the veteran quarterback attempting 49 passes. "Given the numerous injuries at the position and the timing of Valdes-Scantling's release, a reunion with Rodgers felt almost inevitable. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images) Getty Daniel Arwas Wed, October 21, 2026 at 12:03 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have been heavily linked with a certain controversial wide receiver as of late, but it's one of their former players that has made a move to another AFC team. Former deep threat and speedster Marquez Valdes-Scantling, who won two Super Bowl rings with Chiefs during his two-year in 2022 and 2023, has signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers' practice squad, according to the team's official communications on social media. Marquez Valdes-Scantling Signs with Steelers Practice Squad Valdes-Scantling (MVS) started his career in Green Bay before signing a three-year, $30 million deal with the Chiefs in March 2022. Although he struggled with drops earlier in his career; including during his time in Kansas City; he was fairly productive in his two seasons. He managed 1,002 receiving yards and 3 touchdowns off of 62 receptions across those two seasons as the Chiefs won Super Bowl LVII and LVIII. Since then, in less than three years MVS has now spent time on no fewer than 8 different NFL franchises, with his most successful stint having been in 2024 for the New Orleans Saints when he put up 385 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns. Whilst Chiefs fans may still hold resentful feelings towards him for his drops in big moments, most notably against the Philadelphia Eagles back in November 2023, the team won championships in both of his stints with the franchise. So he will forever be enshrined in that memory and as a key member of those historic teams. home.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
home.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. away.headline: NFL Insider Gives Update on 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Achilles Injury
away.blurb: Going into Monday’s game against the Washington Commanders, they were already without wideouts Christian Kirk, De’Zhaun Stribling, DeMarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel Sr. Just before halftime, they lost Mike Evans to an Achilles injury, and he didn’t return. “Mike Evans not being able to finish the game was a big deal for the San Francisco 49ers,” Rapoport said on ESPN. “Went three-and-out, three-and-out, three-and-out. Big reason why was they could not throw it to this guy. “Now, the word was initially at the game, out because of an Achilles. That is like the worst thing you can say. It’s not that. It is Achilles tendinitis that Mike Evans is essentially dealing with, which is something he’s going to continue to deal with. It is something that he’s going to have to manage for the better part of the season. This is the third season in a row where the San Francisco 49ers have had to deal with one injury after another. In particular, their wide receiver room has been hit hard by the injury bug. Evans’ Achilles had already been bothering him for days prior to the game. Without him, the Niners’ offense ground to a halt, but luckily, they had built a 20-3 halftime lead, allowing them to escape with a 23-17 win. Any type of Achilles ailment is scary. After the game, head coach Kyle Shanahan didn’t sound too concerned about Evans’ Achilles, and the injured tendon was reportedly intact. But that doesn’t mean this ailment will heal soon. NFL insider Ian Rapoport said that Evans’ Achilles condition will last for a while . “It is brutal. It does sometimes mean that it leads to other serious injuries. We’ll continue to watch that.” Two seasons ago, Niners running back Christian McCaffrey had a similar condition, and as a result, he didn’t suit up until Week 10. He then suffered a PCL injury three weeks later, and that injury ended his season. Evans has been huge for San Francisco this season. After the team signed him to a three-year deal worth up to $42.4 million during the offseason, he had delivered 27 catches, 420 receiving yards and three touchdowns through six games. He has become a very trusted target for quarterback Brock Purdy, who has made himself a prime MVP candidate. Of Evans’ 27 receptions this year, 25 of them have yielded a first down. The Niners are hoping to get Kirk back from a calf injury this Sunday when they visit the Atlanta Falcons. He hasn’t played yet this year after signing a one-year, $6 million deal with them this offseason. home.blurb: The move comes as Atlanta continues to deal with significant absences at edge rusher. With multiple players unavailable, the Falcons are searching for additional bodies who can contribute and add to this group. The Falcons cannot afford to overlook opportunities to add depth. The lack of healthy and available edge rushers puts more responsibility on the remaining defensive linemen to get after the quarterback. Snowden could help ease some of that burden if he earns a role in the rotation. Snowden, 28, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Virginia in 2021. He previously spent time with the Chicago Bears and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before establishing himself with the Raiders. The Atlanta Falcons are taking a chance on a veteran, signing edge rusher Charles Snowden off the Washington Commanders’ practice squad to their 53-man roster, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. "The Falcons are signing edge Charles Snowden off the Commanders practice squad to their 53-man roster, source said. With Washington this year, Snowden was with the Raiders the last three seasons," Rapoport wrote on X . Josh Kendall of The Athletic reported that edge rusher Bralen Trice was being released in a corresponding move. Trice had burned through his three practice squad elevations and was signed to the 53-man active roster prior to the Bears game. There's a good chance he ends up back on the practice squad and resets his three-game elevation eligibility after clearing waivers. Snowden spent the previous three seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders before joining Washington. He brings NFL experience to a position group that has been hit hard by injuries and suspensions, giving Atlanta another option as it tries to improve its pass rush. However, Snowden also comes with off field concerns. He was arrested last month for DUI and suspended for three games after joining the Dallas Cowboys, making this another calculated risk for a Falcons team that needs help at a position of significant concern. Atlanta’s edge rusher situation has become increasingly difficult to manage. Rookie Jalon Walker is sidelined for the season, while fellow first round pick James Pearce Jr. is serving an eight game suspension, with two games remaining. The Falcons have also placed Yasir Abdullah on injured reserve, while Za’Darius Smith has missed 2 games. Those absences have left Atlanta searching for additional options to help fill the void. During his time in Las Vegas, Snowden appeared in 31 games across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, recording 67 tackles, 12 tackles for loss, and 4.5 sacks. He also recorded an interception during that stretch. He started nine games in each of the previous two years with the Raiders. Those numbers give Atlanta a player with experience contributing at the NFL level, even if he is not a proven premier pass rusher. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Denzel Boston limited at Cleveland Browns practice with injury
away.blurb: The 6-foot-4 pass catcher was still able to practice in a limited capacity, which is a good sign for his availability on Sunday when the Browns take on the Baltimore Ravens. The second-round pick in April's draft leads the NFL with 20.6 yards per reception, while his 330 yards and 3 touchdowns are the best among all rookies. Boston has tallied 16 catches through the first five games of the year and has been a big part of the Browns starting the season at 3-2, which has them tied for second place in the AFC North. However, after pulling in 3 catches for 46 yards and a touchdown against the New York Jets, Boston popped up on Cleveland's injury report on Wednesday with a foot issue. Throughout the year, Boston has made an early impression on the NFL, displaying why he was such a key piece of Jedd Fisch's offense in the head coach's first two seasons on Montlake. "Not making things too big, just keeping the main thing the main thing," Boston said of his poise and early success . "And also just understanding the camaraderie that we built around the building, having the trust that he's going to go make that play or he's going to go make that play. I think it just comes from a great locker room, a brotherhood, and an understanding of everyone's here for their purpose and everyone's going to fulfill their purpose when the time comes." home.blurb: Reports indicate that the 25-year-old sustained a calf injury against the Titans. The Colts announced that Gardner is deemed questionable after notifying the coaching staff that he was dealing with some kind of injury in his left calf. “Sauce Gardner (calf) questionable for return,” the Colts said on X. Gardner left the game after recording just one tackle. That gives him 17 combined tackles (14 solo) and four pass deflections through six games so far this season. With the former first-round pick still out of the game, the Colts have turned to free agent acquisition Cam Taylor-Britt to step in for Gardner. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. Kyler Murray should be able to produce enough offense to let his defense lead them to a win in this interconference duel. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Losing to the Titans at home might be rock bottom. Unfortunately, things get worse starting next Sunday when the Colts travel to Minnesota to take on the Vikings. The 5-0 Vikings… FanDuel Sportsbook agrees that this one will be tough with a +5.5-point spread facing the Colts. The money line begins at +210 while the over/under is 42.5. What a disaster. The Colts let the Titans hang around in the first half and then gave them the game in the second. A fumble on the first play of the third quarter by Jonathan Taylor, paired with another Daniel Jones interception, and a blocked punt for a touchdown to top it all off were too much to overcome. The Colts tied the game late in the fourth but allowed the Tennessee Titans to take and keep the lead. Meanwhile, their opponent is perfect on the year. They may not be a perfect team, but their record remains unblemished after taming the Saints on the road. Only seven points were surrendered by the defense as a fumble return for a touchdown was the only thing making the box score look remotely close. Kyler Murray is getting comfortable, and this defense is insane under Brian Flores. They will be ready to bring the heat on Sunday. The Colts are falling fast. Meeting the Vikings in Minnesota isn't the way to get out of this mess. The Colts struggled to contain the Titans' defense. What are their chances against Minnesota? This could be a tough one to watch.

They’ll be returning to U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 7 to host the Indianapolis Colts, and the folks who get paid to set the betting odds seem to think that they’ll emerge from that game unscathed. Skol! Join Vikings fans on the SB Nation app! Experience every game with fans who understand the excitement—and the stress—of Vikings football. Chat live throughout the game Enjoy fewer ads Jump easily between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Our friends from the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for Week 7 in the NFL, and the Vikings are starting the week as a 5.5-point favorite over the Colts. The over/under for this one has started out at 42.5 points. The Colts had a bit of a rough week in Week 6, as they fell to the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium by a score of 26-20. It was the first victory of the season for the Titans, and the Colts couldn’t get out of their own way all afternoon. They turned the ball over three times, including a pair of interceptions from Daniel Jones, and also had a punt that was blocked by the Titans and returned for a touchdown. That’s how the Colts managed to lose despite holding the Titans to just 186 yards of total offense while blowing a 13-0 halftime lead on their home field. That loss dropped the Colts to 2-4 on the season and has our friends from Stampede Blue calling for their team to “ blow it up .” The Vikings, as we’ve mentioned, are one of three teams in the NFL who are still undefeated at 5-0, along with the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers. The Chiefs climbed to 5-0 by beating the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, while the Niners can get to 6-0 if they defeat the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. The Vikings have done this despite being fairly anemic on offense, thanks to the performance of their defensive and special teams units. In their last game, they overcame two red zone turnovers to defeat the New Orleans Saints by a score of 23-13 in a game that they played without left tackle Christian Darrisaw and wide receiver Jordan Addison, and saw tight end T.J. Hockenson go out on the second play of the game with a concussion. The sportsbooks have spoken, folks, and the Vikings are pretty significant favorites to push their record to 6-0 this week when they face off against the Colts. Does that sound like the right number to you folks? Let us know in the comments. Here’s a Vikings vs Colts prediction. We will look at this from a betting perspective and determine the best Vikings vs Colts pick. Indianapolis Colts Betting Preview The Colts have been a mixed bag for most of the year, and they’ve been mired in fighting off the .500 mark in the record column. Indianapolis started with consecutive losses to the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs, then beat the Houston Texans and Washington Commanders. After a loss to the Steelers Indy was sitting at 2-3 through five games. In last Sunday’s matchup with the Tennessee Titans, the Colts did a bit of scoring in the second quarter and headed into the locker room with a 13-0 lead. Indy gave up 20 unanswered points from there though, and eventually lost a tough one 26-20. QB Daniel Jones was 22-of-42 for 269 yards, one TD and two picks. Johnathan Taylor had 94 rush yards and a score. Minnesota Vikings Betting Preview Over on the Vikings’ side, they rolled into their (pretty early) bye week on a great run. Minnesota opened up the season with five straight victories, taking out the rival Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears in the first two. Next came three more wins over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins and New Orleans Saints for that perfect 5-0 run thus far. Back on October 11 versus the Saints, the Vikings had a couple of field goals in the first half on the way to a 7-6 halftime deficit. Minnesota added a couple more touchdowns and a field goal after that on the way to a 23-13 win. QB Kyler Murray was 24-of-30 for 229 yards and a TD. Aaron Jones led the rush in the victory with 25 carries for 113 yards and a score. Why the Minnesota Vikings will win The Vikings have won each of their last 10 games. The Colts have lost each of their last nine games against opponents on a winning streak. The Vikings have covered the spread in nine of their last 10 October games as favorites against AFC opponents. The Colts have failed to cover the spread in eight of their last nine games as underdogs against NFC opponents. The Vikings have won the first quarter in each of their last five games following a road win. The Vikings have scored the first touchdown in four of their last five games following a road win. The Vikings have won the first half in five of their last six games against teams that held a losing record. The Colts have covered the spread in each of their last four games without Jonathan Taylor. The Vikings have failed to cover the spread in 10 of their last 12 October games at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Colts have won the first quarter in four of their last five games as underdogs against NFC North opponents. The Colts have scored the first touchdown in each of their last eight games following a loss. The Colts have won the first half in seven of their last eight games against the Vikings. Each of the Colts' last six games as road underdogs following a home loss have gone OVER the total points line. Five of the last six Sunday games at U.S. Bank Stadium have gone UNDER the total points line. Jonathan Taylor has recorded 121+ rushing and receiving yards in three of the Colts' last four games following a loss. Heading into Week 7, the Colts have lost the third quarter in each of their last two games – equal-longest active streak in the league. Vikings vs Colts Prediction I’ll lean toward the Vikings. Offensively the Vikings came up with 364 yards and 18 first downs in the 10-point victory. Minnesota is on a nice roll right now but they’re not necessarily blowing teams out to get their wins. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor, running back Jaylen Wright and receiver Caleb Douglas also sat out. Because it was a bye-week session, some absences may have been precautionary. The Jets' Friday report belongs to their Week 6 game, not the Miami matchup. Breece Hall, guard Dylan Parham, receiver Adonai Mitchell and edge rusher Joseph Ossai were listed out after missing practice with injuries. Safety Dane Belton and tight end Kenyon Sadiq carried questions, while Omar Cooper Jr. entered a return window from injured reserve. Whatever happens in New York's game this weekend will become the starting point for its Miami report. The matchup implications are significant. If Savaiinaea cannot return, Jarrett Kingston is the likely replacement against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. If Brents, Taylor or Duck remain unavailable, Miami will again ask young defensive backs to cover Garrett Wilson. If Hall's quadriceps injury lingers, Braelon Allen would become New York's primary runner. Cornerbacks Storm Duck and Darrell Baker Jr., edge defender Trey Moore and other eligible players may become options when game-week practice begins. De'Von Achane remains on injured reserve with a knee injury and is not expected to play against New York. Gordon therefore remains the lead back, with Wright and Kaytron Allen behind him if healthy. The first official Dolphins-Jets injury report is expected next Wednesday. Until then, this is a watch list, not a final designation sheet.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. Tampa Bay opened as a three-point underdog on the road in Week 7, and it has since moved to a 3.5-point underdog in the latest odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. At 1-5, the Bucs are +570 to make the playoffs and +12500 to win the Super Bowl, making them one of the bigger long shots in the NFL through six weeks. Mayfield has appeared in just three games and didn't exactly play at a high level, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards, two scores and two picks before suffering the thumb injury. He's also carried the ball 11 times for 65 yards and a score this season. Tampa Bay's practice report on Wednesday should provide more insight into Mayfield's status for Week 7. away.headline: New report reveals when Baker Mayfield could return for Buccaneers
away.blurb: Baker Mayfield Eyeing Return for Panthers Game? NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that there's "optimism" in Tampa Bay that Mayfield could return for the team's Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers. This return timeline makes sense for a lot of reasons, however. To begin, Bowles' initial assessment of Mayfield's injury was three weeks minimum — it will be past that assessment once the Bucs play the Steelers this Sunday, so Mayfield's window has opened up. Additionally, this will be Tampa Bay's first NFC South game. The team, despite being 1-4, is one and a half games out of the NFC South lead, so it's crucial to gain some ground in that division. Tampa Bay will want its starting quarterback out there when it does, so it's understandable that Mayfield would try to get back in time for it. Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Rules Out 2 Players vs. Steelers This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/buccaneers/onsi as New Report Reveals When Baker Mayfield Could Return for Buccaneers . The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will look to improve to 2-4 on the year when they face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. When they do, they won't be playing their starting quarterback. Undrafted free agent rookie has been deputizing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for the last two games as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. Daniels hasn't been bad in the role, and he's set to play another game on Sunday under center as Mayfield continues to recover. This is Mayfield's team, though, and the team's three-year, $165 million extension of him this offseason proves it. Mayfield has been itching to get back to action ever since his injury, and one NFL insider pinpointed the exact game that could happen — and it's coming up very soon. Mayfield tried to throw on Wednesday afternoon after Bucs practice. It's unknown how that throwing session went, but the team clearly did not think he was ready enough to get back to practice this week, so Daniels gets the start once again for Tampa Bay. Finally, Mayfield used to play for Carolina in 2022, and the experience was an overall negative one for him. He's made it very clear that he pays particular attention to revenge games on the schedule, so there's probably some extra incentive there as well. Before he got hurt, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He's struggled in a few different respects, though, as he's fumbled the ball three times this year and lost all of them. He'll look to bounce back from his recent stretch of play when he gets back under center for the Bucs. Tampa Bay — led by Daniels — will play the Steelers on Sunday at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium. But don't expect Mayfield to be away for long. away.headline: Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield may try to return from injury for Panthers game
away.blurb: It sounds like Mayfield could attempt to return to the lineup when the Buccaneers play at the 3-2 Carolina Panthers on Oct. 25. Bowles previously said that Mayfield would likely be sidelined for "a minimum of three weeks" due to his setback, but a subsequent report noted that the signal-caller wanted to return after just two missed games. Such a scenario didn't play out, but Ira Kaufman of the JoeBucsFan website noted on Monday that "even Baker Mayfield detractors can’t muster a sensible argument to keep him sidelined once he is healed from a dislocated right thumb" following what happened at Tampa Bay's Raymond James Stadium on Sunday afternoon. A Tampa Bay Buccaneers side that has been without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield since he went down with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand in Week 3 fell to 1-5 on the season when it squandered a 16-3 lead en route to suffering a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Buccaneers will evaluate Baker Mayfield "during the week" ahead of Panthers game Per Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles confirmed on Monday that Mayfield is on track to practice this coming Wednesday. "He’s supposed to practice Wednesday," Bowles said about Mayfield. "We’re gonna take a good look at him there, and we’ll kind of evaluate him during the week and see how he does." U ndrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has served as Tampa Bay's temporary QB1 since the club's Week 4 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Oct. 4. While Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown to help Tampa Bay earn a stunning 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 8, he came back down to earth when he tossed a pair of interceptions and took five sacks in the Buccaneers' loss to the Steelers. Buccaneers will try to get Baker Mayfield, Jalon Daniels ready for Panthers game "Both will be in the meetings, obviously," Bowles added about Mayfield and Daniels. "Both will be in the meetings, and we’ll see how the week goes before we decide who it is." After Bowles offered his Mayfield update, DraftKings Sportsbook had the Buccaneers on Monday as three-point underdogs against the Panthers. Want more articles like this? As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. away.headline: Bengals injuries make early bye week a sudden positive
away.blurb: We’ll see how this plays out once the Bengals go through that 12-game gauntlet and potentially into the playoffs. But now that it’s here, the timing of the bye week doesn’t seem too bad, after all. When the NFL announced the schedule, the Cincinnati Bengals sitting with a Week 6 bye looked like a negative. That early bye week means 12 games in a row through next January to close the season. Five of those are away from home and one is overseas in Madrid, Spain, with kickoff set for a 9:30 a.m. ET start time. Seemed rough, but as the Bengals sit on that bye week right now…it’s actually pretty perfect timing. Just ask Bengals head coach Zac Taylor. "I think that was your gut reaction when you first saw (the schedule). When the bye was. Man, you kind of like it more towards Thanksgiving," Taylor said, according to Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "But I do think just where our team is right now and the way that these last three games have gone down to the wire and guys playing through some stuff right now, it is a good time to get the bye and get our legs back underneath us, get some guys healthy, and go full force when we come back for Baltimore." … Keep in mind that before this break, big names like Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were frequents on the injury report already. Better to let those guys rest up than risk aggravating something even worse. Even Joe Burrow was dealing with back soreness early in the season and jammed a finger during the pre-bye win in Miami. This article originally appeared on Bengals Wire: Bengals injuries make early bye week a sudden positive

away.headline: Cincinnati Bengals Terminate Rookie Contract in Sudden Move
away.blurb: Nwokobia, an undrafted free agent out of SMU, originally signed with the Bengals in early May following the 2026 NFL Draft. With established safeties Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle, and Kyle Dugger ahead of him, plus depth pieces such as PJ Jules and the newly promoted Yeast, opportunities on the active roster have been limited for undrafted rookies. Nwokobia is now a free agent and eligible to sign with another team or return to Cincinnati should circumstances change. Eagles rule Jalen Hurts out for season amid blood clot issues Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The Cincinnati Bengals released rookie safety Isaiah Nwokobia from the practice squad on Tuesday, according to a team announcement detailing multiple roster adjustments. The move came as the Bengals signed safety Russ Yeast from the practice squad to the active roster. Yeast fills a spot opened by tight end Tanner Hudson’s placement on injured reserve. To replenish the practice squad, Cincinnati signed tight end Josh Kattus and linebacker Emany Johnson. The 23-year-old from Dallas (Skyline High School) brought solid college production: career totals of 273 tackles, 11 interceptions (two returned for touchdowns), and 14 pass deflections across 53 games. He earned first-team All-ACC honors in 2024 after recording 100 tackles and three interceptions, and was named MVP of the 2023 American Athletic Conference Championship Game. His path with the Bengals has been uneven. The team waived him early in training camp on August 4 amid an undisclosed injury, with Nwokobia later reaching an injury settlement. He returned to the organization on September 29 when Cincinnati signed him to the practice squad after a workout. The latest release ends that stint. Nwokobia’s early camp release already suggested the Bengals viewed the position as relatively settled, and the current secondary depth appears to have left little room for further development on the practice squad. No specific reason for the practice-squad release was detailed beyond the corresponding roster moves. For a productive college safety who showed ball skills and tackling ability, the short NFL window underscores the steep competition at the position across the league. away.headline: Bengals Get Key Injury Updates Ahead of Ravens Matchup in Week 7
away.blurb: Wide receiver Colbie Young, a fourth-round pick out of Georgia, suffered a knee injury in week three and missed the Bengals' games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Miami Dolphins. Andrei Iosivias's injury forced Dohnte Meyers into the wide receiver three role just a couple of months after receiving a training camp invite after playing in the CFL last season. Cincinnati also signed Mitchell Tinsley off the Houston Texans' practice squad. The Ravens face a significant injury report this week, as quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed the last two games, in which Baltimore went 1-1, beating the Atlanta Falcons and losing to the Cleveland Browns. Jackson has been labeled day-to-day and could return for a big divisional rivalry game. Bengals Get Key Injury Updates Ahead of Ravens Matchup in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Bengals Get Key Injury Updates Ahead of Ravens Matchup in Week 7 (Frank Bowen IV/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 5:49 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Week seven is here, and the Cincinnati Bengals will play their second AFC North game of the season with a chance to establish themselves atop the division. Cincinnati is 3-2 and last in the division, while the Cleveland Browns, Pittsburgh Steelers, and Ravens are all 4-2. Cincinnati is getting in much better shape injury-wise. The week before the Miami Dolphins game, the Bengals were unsure whether Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins , or Bryan Cook could play after earlier injuries. This week, they won't have to worry about which starters will play, barring any practice setbacks. Safety Kyle Dugger returned to practice after missing the last two games against the Jaguars and Dolphins. Dugger is a depth option at safety behind Bryan Cook and Jordan Battle. He has five solo tackles for the season and provides a veteran presence on the back end of the Bengals' defense. Defensive end Cashius Howell missed practice due to illness, and his status will be worth monitoring this week. If he misses one or two more days, the question will be whether he's physically ready to play against the Ravens. He's been a big contributor on the defensive line, racking up 12 pressures in his rookie year, second among all NFL rookies. Howell was one of five defensive line additions this offseason, the only one from the top three rounds of the NFL Draft. The other three, Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe, and Jonathan Allen, were either traded for or signed as free agents. Cincinnati is very high on Young after a great training camp, and his frame projects as a possible replacement for Tee Higgins. With injuries around Cincinnati's receivers, Young will get a good number of snaps if he returns in week seven.
