Cincinnati won 13-7, shutting out the Ravens until the final minutes of the game. (AP Photo/Al Behrman) Ravens Bengals Week 7 Opponent Preview Scouting Report Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Michael Hull Digital Coordinator Fresh off a Week 6 bye, the Cincinnati Bengals head to Baltimore for an AFC North battle with the Ravens. Baltimore is coming off a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 and sits at 4-2 on the year. The Ravens offense ranks seventh in the NFL with 26 points per game and eighth with 367.7 yards per game under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. Franchise QB Lamar Jackson has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, and backup Tyler Huntley has led the Ravens to a 1-1 record in Jackson's absence. First-year Head Coach Jesse Minter said Monday he is unsure if Jackson returns to practice or plays this week against the Bengals. "I'd still put it in kind of the day-to-day thing," Minter said. "We'll know a lot more on Wednesday, I would say." When he has been on the field, Jackson has completed 70.8% of his passes (68-of-96) for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. Meanwhile, Huntley has also completed 70.8% of his passes (51-of-72) for 429 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. The offense has been less vertical in two games with Huntley: Jackson leads all quarterbacks with at least 25 attempts in average yards per attempt (10.1) this season, while Huntley ranks 35th among 43 QBs (6.0), per NFL NextGenStats. RB Derrick Henry continues to defy Father Time as he leads the NFL in carries (130), is tied for first in rushing touchdowns (seven) and is fourth in rushing yards (534) in his age-32 season. He also forced 29 missed tackles, the sixth most in the league. WR Zay Flowers again leads the Baltimore receiving room. Despite missing Week 2, Flowers ranks ninth in the NFL with 471 receiving yards. Among 218 pass catchers to run at least 50 routes this season, Flowers ranks first in yards per route run (3.8). In two matchups with the Bengals last year, CB DJ Turner II matched up with Flowers 21 times, allowing one catch for 14 yards on four targets, per NGS. Help us honor 2026 Ring of Honor inductees James Brooks and Bob Trumpy at halftime against the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 1! Baltimore is allowing 22 points per game defensively, the 15th fewest in the NFL, and giving up 310.8 yards per game, the 12th fewest. Former Bengal Trey Hendrickson highlights the Baltimore defense, ranking in the top 12 in QB pressures with 25 so far this season. Hendrickson returned from injury in last week's loss to the Browns to record eight pressures and a sack. His 22.7% pressure percentage ranks third among edge rushers with at least 25 pass rush snaps per NGS. The Ravens have allowed 210.

away.blurb: Bengals tease good news coming out of bye week regarding two injured players while Ravens give brief Lamar Jackson update Skip to content It turns out the bye week came at the perfect time for the Cincinnati Bengals with a monumental AFC North matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on deck. Colbie Young's return is imminent as well At wide receiver, rookie Colbie Young is also on track to returning very soon. Taylor said the 24 year-old looks “ as good as he has in a long time .” Young was close to playing in Week 5 against the Dolphins. He suffered his knee injury on the first offensive play of Cincinnati's Week 3 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. His injury pave the way for Mitch Tinsley to return to the club. His return would put the Bengals on the doorstep of being fully healthy at the position. Andrei Iosivas coming back would complete the group. Iosivas needs to sit out at least one more game before he's eligible to come off of I.R. The Bengals have not had their full receiving corps since Week 2. Cincinnati Bengals’ updated list of pending 2027 free agents at the bye week reveals several key players are playing out contract seasons College Football Close Menu All College Football Kyle Dugger looks close to returning Taylor made it clear last week after Cincinnati's 31-24 victory over the Miami Dolphins that only a few players would be dealing with injuries that could impact them in Week 7 and beyond. Two of those players, linebacker Swayze Bozeman and tight end Tanner Hudson, have been placed on the Reserve/Injured list. The other one is safety Kyle Dugger, who was declared as week-to-week with his quad injury. Dugger did practice for the first time in weeks Monday, signaling progress towards him being able to suit up in the near future. “I think he's progressing along,” Taylor said of Dugger Monday afternoon . “We'll kind of see where he's at.” Cincinnati has leaned on fellow backup S PJ Jules in the two games Dugger has missed. S Russ Yeast has also been elevated from the practice squad in Dugger's absence. Cincinnati will release its first injury report of the week on Wednesday. It sounds like it should be a relatively clean list to start the week. The main injury storyline for this week revolves around Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Baltimore lost its starting QB two weeks ago to an ankle sprain. Tyler Huntley is 1-1 in his place. When asked for an update on Jackson, Ravens coach Jesse Minter continues to label him as “ day-to-day ,” claiming he can “potentially” play Sunday against Cincinnati. He said that Jackson has made progress, but obviously wants to keep things vague early in the week. Jackson has won 11 of his 13 starts against the Bengals. While he's never played this version of Cincinnati's defense, the Bengals know exactly the kind of threat he possesses. Cornerback DJ Turner II confirmed they are preparing for Jackson to start . away.blurb: The 2024 Big Ten Kicker of the Year was tasked with launching the kickoff out of the back of the end zone before the two-minute warning, which would have saved the Giants about 40 seconds for one last comeback drive. He came up short. The ball was returned, and the clock whittled down to 2:00. Young J.J. McCarthy indeed needed that additional time to score a touchdown. Zvada should be able to come through in that spot, but he is a rookie. Harbaugh could also have ceded five yards by kicking the ball out of bounds, keeping the clock the same. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/giants/onsi as Giants Rookie Report Card Week 6: J.C. Davis Impresses in Limited Action . The New York Giants squandered much of the trust they built early in the campaign after a rough 34-27 loss to the visiting New Orleans Saints. While there were some thrilling moments and impressive performances, the overall picture was quite ugly. Big Blue’s rookies were largely underwhelming. First-year players will experience growing pains, and those can happen even against a sub .500 squad at home. Let’s take a look at where the rookies stand after a frustrating Week 6. The Giants were cautious with left tackle Andrew Thomas after he was evaluated for a concussion , so they gave sixth-round draft pick J.C. Davis an extended look. The former Illinois standout picked up where he left off in the summer and made many fans wonder why he wasn’t already on the active offensive line. Davis allowed no sacks, pressures, or hurries in 25 offensive snaps , according to Pro Football Focus. He also stayed penalty-free, which was not an easy thing to do on this day. The Giants still have run-blocking issues, but Davis’ pass-protection skills could be invaluable if Thomas misses time again. Even when the No. 5 overall pick has a down game, he still manages to produce at least one memorable play. Arvell Reese’s highlight against the Saints came when he effortlessly forced offensive lineman David Edwards to the ground, which in turn caused running back Kendre Miller to trip about midway through the second quarter. Reese posted four total stops, but he showed his inexperience with two missed tackles . While the combination of speed and strength is eye-catching, he is still learning what it means to be an NFL linebacker. The sixth-round linebacker has not seen the field on defense, but he remains a consistent presence on special teams. Jack Kelly logged a season-high 31 snaps against the Saints, per PFF, and has now totaled at least 24 in three straight games. He is doing the unglamorous work that is helping the Giants become a more balanced team. The special teams unit was far from its best, but Kelly has earned a weekly role, which is more than coaches can reasonably expect from a Day 3 selection. home.blurb: Texans WR Tank Dell to return from gruesome 2024 knee injury on Sunday vs. Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL "I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel . Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments , sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since. Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston. Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here. Ryan Young Staff writer Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024. Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome. He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day. The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally. Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

away.headline: Week 6 Injury Report: Seahawks at Broncos
away.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). Starting cornerback Riley Moss, who missed last weekend's game with a rib injury, is questionable after being listed as limited in practice all week. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee, limited participation) CB Riley Moss (ribs, limited participation) Tuesday's injury report, which like Monday's is an estimation of participation, was mostly unchanged from a day earlier. Guard Beau Stephens (shoulder) went from being listed as limited Monday to full participation Tuesday, while every other player's status stayed the same. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, was listed as limited for the second straight day due to an ankle injury, as was defensive tackle Leonard Williams. Receiver Irv Charles, who was activated from injured reserve earlier in the day, was again listed as a full participant, another indicator that he is on track to make his Seahawks debut on Thursday. For the Broncos, two starters in the secondary, cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were listed as non-participants for the second straight day. The only change for the Broncos from Monday to Tuesday was defensive end Sai'vion Jones improving from limited to full participation with a shoulder injury. The Seahawks did not practice Tuesday; practice report is an estimation. A Thursday night game in Denver means the Seahawks and Broncos were both required to put out their first injury report of the week on Monday even though neither team actually practiced. The Seahawks' estimated practice report had two players listed as not practicing, linebacker Chazz Surratt, who has missed the past two games with a calf injury, and linebacker Drake Thomas, who injured his ankle in Sunday's loss to the 49ers, but was able to return to the game. New to the injury report this week was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited with an ankle injury, but was able to finish Sunday's game. home.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. The Packers opened the week as underdogs, getting 1.5 points at most sportsbooks, but the line quickly flipped to Packers -1.5 by Monday morning. Then, once the dust settled and the game approached, at least a handful of books had switched back to having the Cowboys favored. The Packers cruised, however, earning a convincing 23-13 victory to move to 4-2 on the season. That record puts them in second place in the NFC North, 1.5 games behind the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings and a half-game up on the 3-2 Detroit Lions. Both of those two teams were idle in Week 6, but the Packers have a chance to make some significant movement in the division next Sunday. Week 7 brings the Packers their third game against an NFC North opponent this season, as they will travel to Detroit to play the Lions in the late Sunday afternoon time slot. Look for that game to be FOX's game of the week, particularly with the Packers' recent resurgence back into serious playoff contention. However, the books are giving the Lions a reasonable advantage in this game thanks to it being played on their own home turf. FanDuel sportsbook opened the line at Lions -3.5 for next Sunday in the first of two meetings between these teams in 2026. Books are also expecting another high-scoring game between these two squads, setting the over/under for total points at 52.5. Last year saw the Packers sweep Detroit for the first time since Dan Campbell took over as Lions head coach. Green Bay took the season opener at Lambeau Field 27-13, then got another Thanksgiving Day victory in Detroit in a high-scoring, 31-24 affair. Prior to 2025, the 2020 season was the last time Green Bay went 2-for-2, when they won similarly high scoring games in weeks 2 (42-24) and 14 (also 31-24). The Detroit Lions (3-2) will host their division rival Green Bay Packers (4-2) in Week 7, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -3.5 points . The Packers finished their 2025 season by snagging the seven seed in the playoffs, but the Bears eliminated them in the Wild Card round. Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley was hired to be the next head coach of the Miami Dolphins, and Green Bay hired Jonathan Gannon (previously the head coach of the Cardinals) as a replacement. With Gannon came a new 3-4 defense and a whole bunch of changes on the defensive side of the ball. EDGE Rashan Gary was traded to the Cowboys, NT Colby Wooden was traded to the Colts, while EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, MIKE Quay Walker, and CB Nate Hobbs departed in free agency. EDGE/LB Micah Parsons continues to recover from an ACL tear and is not expected to be available in Week 7. Being up against the cap, the Packers elected to promote from within, inserting EDGE Lukas Van Ness and ILB Isaiah McDuffie into the starting lineup, trading for LB Zaire Franklin (who is starting in place of injured Edgerrin Cooper), and drafting starters CB Brandon Cisse (second round) and NT Chris McClellan (third) on Day 2 of the NFL Draft. On offense, the Packers lost QB Malik Willis, RB Emanuel Wilson, WR Dontayvion Wicks (traded to the Eagles), WR Romeo Dobbs, LT Rasheed Walker, and LG/C Elgton Jenkins; like on defense, they elected to mostly promote from within, elevating RB Marshawn Lloyd into a bigger role (especially with Josh Jacobs suspended—he is expected to return in Week 7), WR Savion Williams and LT Jordan Morgan into the starting lineup, and shifting Sean Rhyan inside to center. Their guard spots have been a massive problem, and the Packers have been searching for answers, with their most recent pairing being RG Travis Glover and former Lion LG Laken Tomlinson (starting in place of the injured Aaron Banks). After a slow start to their 2026 season, the Packers have settled down as their offense has found its groove. The Packers opened the season with a loss after allowing the Vikings to drop 39 points on them, rebounded in Week 2 by beating the Jets by three points, only to lose again in Week 3 as the Falcons dominated them on the ground to the tune of 35 points. In Week 4, the Packers once again found a way to win by three points, this time over the Bucs, then smashed a Caleb Williams-less Bears team 31-7. In Week 6, the Packers took on the Cowboys’ 31st-ranked defense on “Sunday Night Football,” and while they jumped out to a 17-0 lead in the first half, they only scored six points in the second half. Fortunately, their defense held strong and allowed only 13 points, and the game ended in a 23-13 win. With the Packers offense in a groove, the Lions secondary is certainly going to be tested. Will they be able to carry over the success they had against the Cardinals in Week 5? Will Brian Branch return? If so, how big of a factor will he be? With so much unknown about the Lions’ defense, there’s a real chance the Packers continue their run of putting up points, and Detroit will need their top-scoring offense to keep pace and lead the Lions to victory. Detroit Lions Bring Back Aidan Keanaaina Keanaaina originally signed with Detroit as an undrafted free agent following the 2026 NFL Draft after playing college football at Notre Dame and California. The 6-foot-3, 320-pound defensive tackle showed enough promise to earn an opportunity with the Lions before suffering an injury during training camp. Detroit placed Keanaaina on injured reserve in August before eventually reaching an injury settlement with the rookie. With that settlement period behind him, the Lions have now decided to bring him back into the organization. As we reported Monday , Keanaaina recently visited the Lions as the team evaluated potential defensive-line additions. Tuesday's official announcement confirms Detroit has decided to move forward with the reunion. During his final college season at California, Keanaaina recorded 56 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks . His size and experience defending the interior make him an intriguing developmental option for a Lions team looking to maintain depth along its defensive front. Chris Smith Released From Lions Practice Squad Smith had spent the first six weeks of the 2026 season on Detroit's practice squad without receiving a game-day elevation. Despite earning praise from Dan Campbell for his work ethic and attention to detail, the Lions have decided to move in another direction. away.headline: Packers-Cowboys Thursday Injury Report: (Really) Big Help on the Way
away.blurb: Riley was designated for return from the PUP list on Wednesday and went through his second practice on Thursday. While he probably will need more than one week of practice, he will be a huge asset – literally and figuratively – whenever he’s cleared for game action. “Definitely rusty,” he said after being limited participation at practice. “Just trying to knock the rust off. We got a saying, ‘Got to vs. get to.’ I get to get coached. I get to get those reps in practice, which are very expensive, as I like to say, expensive reps. So, I take those very seriously and it's been good. I’m good physically. No sores or aches. I’m just in a good spot. Taking it day by day at a time.” “Man, it sucks, but it’s part of the business,” he said. “It’s part of the game we play. We love to play. You can’t really be so stuck on the past. You just got to continue to look forward, so when it happened, I just knew I’m going to recover from an Achilles injury. Few seconds to get down a little bit, but after that’s over, the emotion’s over, I told myself I’m going to return from an Achilles injury.” The Packers need help on the defensive line. It was one of their strongest positions coming out of training camp but Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and he’ll soon be joined by Hargrave. That leaves the Packers with only five players at a position group in which coordinator Jonathan Gannon prefers to rotate players in and out of the lineup. “That is above me,” he said of his potential return. “I just stick on one day at a time. Today, we had padded practice, so that’s what my focus was on – padded practice today. No really looking forward; just taking it each day at a time.” Cornerback Keisean Nixon and defensive tackle Jonathan Ford did not practice on Wednesday. Nixon returned on Thursday and was limited participation. home.headline: Cade Mays’ return gives Lions an offensive line dilemma
home.blurb: Center Cade Mays is returning from a wrist injury this week that’s kept him out since August, and it’ll force some interesting conversations about what to do with Juice Scruggs– who has been playing very well in his stead. Some might say it’s the easy call to ride with the hot hand. But the Lions paid Mays to be their starter— his 3-year, $25 million deal was the only starter money they handed out this offseason. Lions face a tough Week 7 decision amid Mays' return As a whole, Detroit’s offensive line looks vastly improved this year, and much closer to the vaunted units the team rolled out from 2022 to 2024. But 2025 was a disastrous year for the Lions in the trenches, and should serve as a stark reminder of how important it is for them to get this group right. Tate Ratledge has been stout this year at right guard and the Lions invested a second round pick in him last year, so you’ve got to think left guard Christian Mahogany would be the odd man out if the Lions were to put both Scruggs and Mays in the lineup. Mays’ return gives the Lions some needed depth at the very least with Ben Bartch on injured reserve. And Scruggs and Mahogany’s good play means they don’t have to rush Mays back or overload him when he’s not ready. The Lions would probably tell you this situation is more of a luxury than it is a dilemma— but they’ve still got to figure it out. That starting lineup when they host the Green Bay Packers this week will be a fascinating one to look out for. 2 pros and 3 cons to Lions' plan for a center rotation thanks to Cade Mays' return Josh Jacobs’s return gives Lions another reason to worry about the Packers in Week 7 It's now or never for Lions' defense with Brian Branch's return imminent This article was originally published on sidelionreport.com as Cade Mays’ return gives Lions an offensive line dilemma . For the first time in what feels like an eternity, the Detroit Lions find themselves with a good problem to have at offensive line. You would be forgiven for thinking Scruggs was little more than a throw-in in the David Montgomery trade the Lions made with the Houston Texans. But when Mays went down, Scruggs assumed the starting role. It’s gone better than anyone could have expected. Scruggs is currently Pro Football Focus’ No. 2 graded center in football. He’s anchored Detroit’s running game and been a menace in pass protection. In his press conference Monday, it didn’t really seem like head coach Dan Campbell quite knew what to do. “That's the hard thing. Juice is playing pretty good football for us right now. He's done a good job. He's gotten better every week,” Campbell said . ”Juice is a freaking team guy. It doesn't mean that if it comes to that, that he doesn't like that. home.headline: It's now or never for Lions' defense with Brian Branch's return imminent
home.blurb: It's now or never for Lions' defense with Brian Branch's return imminent Skip to main content News The return of safety Brian Branch is a critical point for this defense. If it shows some improvement with its do-it-all DB back in the lineup from a torn Achilles, the Lions have something to build on. That should make them buyers at the November 10 trade deadline. If it's still among the NFL's worst units, then Detroit can basically kiss any hopes of meaningful contention goodbye. The defense has been flat-out unworkable in multiple games this season. Before last week, it ranked near the bottom of the league in most conventional and advanced statistics. Brian Branch's imminent return could help transform Lions' defense This was what the Lions needed to see entering their bye week with one of their most impactful players potentially nearing a return. Abney hadn't played safety since middle school, and almost exclusively played outside cornerback in college. But the Lions tried him at nickel before kicking him back to safety against Arizona – partly out of necessity and partly because it couldn't get any worse. The Detroit Lions' defense is about to have a make-or-break moment. The Lions still allow the most yards per game in the NFL and the fourth-highest points per game. But yes, last Sunday's win over the lowly Arizona Cardinals was a good sign of a turnaround – or at the very least, that Detroit has nowhere to go but up defensively. The Lions sacked quarterback Jacoby Brissett five times, and he completed just 29 of his 47 passing attempts. Arizona rushed for just 56 yards as a team on 18 attempts. Yes, the Cardinals are one of the worst teams in the NFL. But the Lions were at a point, following their loss to the Carolina Panthers, where it looked like their defense was going to get in trouble from just about every offense in the NFL. After a slow first-quarter start, it's nice to see any encouraging results from this unit. "I thought we were sticky in coverage, very disciplined minus a couple of plays there," head coach Dan Campbell said . "I thought (defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard) and the staff did an outstanding job and the players really responded, man. They took it to heart and tried to do all the little things right, and play with aggressiveness, and just really set the tone for the day." Branch is a Swiss Army knife to the extreme on defense. His fusion of man coverage stickiness, zone coverage feel, blitz ferocity, sure tackling, and run defense instincts is unmatched by just about anyone in the NFL. Offenses absolutely have to know where he is. His versatility makes everyone on the Lions' defense's job easier. When he's at his best, Branch is a truly transformative player. It doesn't seem like fellow safety Kerby Joseph is returning from his mysterious knee injury anytime soon, or ever. That means Branch could be paired with rookie Keith Abney at safety. picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.headline: Rams sign former Super Bowl champion to be their new kicker
away.blurb: Grupe, whom the Rams signed to replace Harrison Mevis, tore his ACL in his debut with the team on Sunday while trying to make a tackle. He made a 44-yard field goal before getting injured, but he's now ruled out for the season. The Los Angeles Rams will have another new kicker this week when they take on the Las Vegas Raiders , which will be their third in as many games. The Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus to replace the injured Blake Grupe . McManus won Super Bowl 50 as a member of the Denver Broncos and has kicked in the NFL for 12 years, with this season being his 13th. He spent nine years with the Broncos, one with the Jacksonville Jaguars and the last two with the Green Bay Packers . McManus, 35, went 24-for-30 as the Packers' kicker in 2025, with a long of 56 yards. He was just 6-for-12 from beyond 50 yards, including 3 of 7 from 40-49 yards. McManus will be the Rams' third kicker of the season, and hopefully the last. Los Angeles' special teams unit has been the worst in the NFL and it desperately needs some stability from a veteran like McManus. McManus has had his share of down years, including 2017 when he only made 75% of his field goal attempts and 2022 when he made 77.8%, but he was 20-for-21 as recently as 2024, good for a 95.2% make rate. That's the version of McManus the Rams need right now as they head into a crucial part of their season. home.headline: NFL suspends Bills safety Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Raiders
home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, he re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn't rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. The Bills reached out to White a few weeks ago and targeted the bye week for his return. Buffalo opened up a practice squad spot by releasing cornerback A.J. Woods. ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardiner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardiner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardiner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons, and signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson's spitting act as being “inexcusable," and said he's discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can't happen. That's not what we're about. That's not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don't need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can't happen. It won't happen again. Personality-wise, I'm not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills announced they're bringing back a familiar face by signing cornerback Tre'Davious White to their practice squad. The 31-year-old White returns for what would be a third stint in Buffalo, and provide the Bills secondary with some much-needed experience. White was selected by Buffalo in the first round of the 2017 draft, and spent his first seven seasons with the Bills before his career was derailed by injuries. See AP’s full NFL coverage here

However, there is one big issue for the Raiders right now: their running game. While their run blocking has been suspect, the Raiders also have a problem with star second-year running back Ashton Jeanty through six weeks of the season. As ESPN's Ryan McFadden highlighted, the Raiders might have a real problem with Jeanty right now. As he put it, after Week 6 against the Buffalo Bills , "the alarm bells around Jeanty have gotten louder." Raiders might have an Ashton Jeanty problem "Jeanty's rushing numbers this season have been subpar for a player taken inside the top 10 of last year's draft," McFadden writes. "At this point, the Raiders need to consider increasing Mike Washington Jr.'s workload." The Raiders invested heavily in Jeanty in the 2025 NFL Draft, taking him inside the top-10 with the hope he'd become a franchise-saving RB like what Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs have turned into with their respective franchises. But after Week 6, the concern for Jeanty cannot keep being ignored. There have been some worries going around for five weeks, but another lackluster performance has put Jeanty on notice. Washington, the rookie backup running back, ran the ball nine times for 43 yards, looking a lot more explosive. This season, Jeanty has 313 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown on 98 attempts, good for 3.19 yards per carry. That's not good enough, especially with Washington at 4.94 yards per carry sitting behind him. While the Raiders have made it clear they're not going to rest Jeanty for a week in hopes of his ankle injury from the preseason getting better, it should be clear to the Raiders now that they should turn this backfield into more of a split one if Jeanty isn't going to rest. The concern with Jeanty is real, and if his struggles continue, which they very well might with the Los Angeles Rams next on their schedule, it might be time for a change in the Raiders' backfield. Both of these teams have playoff expectations in 2026, but they’re in very different spots through six weeks of the season. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs +2.5 (-115) Seahawks -2.5 (-105) Seahawks: -135 42.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The Seahawks opened as just 1.5-point favorites in Week 7 , but the line has already moved to Seattle -2.5. There is clearly some confidence in this Seattle defense with an extended rest at home against Kansas City. The Chiefs have not lost this season, but they are banged up at the receiver position with Rashee Rice missing Week 6 and Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Oddsmakers seem to think this is a spot where the Chiefs will lose their first game in 2026. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Betting Preview These are two of the best defenses in the league, which isn’t what you’d usually think about when referring to a Patrick Mahomes-led squad. The Chiefs traded away Trent McDuffie in the offseason, yet they’re third in the league in EPA/Play and success rate and fourth in EPA/Pass. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.headline: Cyrus Allen, Andrew Armstrong proved to be part of the Kansas City Chiefs' answer at wide receiver after Week 6 win over Chargers
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs leaned on a practice squad call-up and a rookie with Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve and Rashee Rice sidelined. Here’s what stood out from their Week 6 snaps. The Kansas City Chiefs had new wide receiver contributors in their Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. With Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve and Rashee Rice out with a hamstring injury, Kansas City leaned more on practice squad wide receiver Andrew Armstrong , rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen, and second-year wide receiver Jalen Royals than in any game this season. "Yeah, they did good,” Mahomes said. “They played fast. There were some learning moments here and there, but at the end of the day I thought they played hard. They played fast. They blocked when they needed to block, and they made the catches whenever they got the ball thrown their way, and so they’ll continue to get more and more involved in the offense, and obviously, not having the guys out there, it's accelerated their growth a little bit, but I always have a lot of confidence in those guys.” It was a good start for the young players as their roles begin to ramp up. Rice could be back as early as Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks. Even so, Kansas City still has some things to figure out at the position. “It was great,” Armstrong said after the game. “Just going out there in practice, earning the trust from the quarterback, earning the trust from coaches, earning the trust from my teammates. And just making sure that we go out there and I can trust them, they can trust me, and it was great.” The stat sheet shows only one reception on two targets for 13 yards, but Armstrong ran the third-most routes of any Chiefs receiver with 24. He served as one of the team’s primary perimeter receivers. What stood out most was one of the traits that also defined his preseason: his run-blocking ability . Allen had limited opportunities against Los Angeles, playing just nine offensive snaps. Leading into the game, expectations were that he might take on a larger role. Instead, his usage was about the same as before the injuries to Thornton and Rice. His 23-yard reception on first-and-20 in the fourth quarter is the best example of that trust. Mahomes threw the ball across the middle of the field with a linebacker trailing in coverage. The pass was fantastic, and Allen’s execution on the grab helped the Chiefs extend their lead and put the game firmly out of reach. A tough Week 7 matchup against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks awaits. It stands to reason that both Armstrong and Allen could get more chances to make an impact and prove they’re part of the solution. For now, the Chiefs will keep sorting through their wide receivers as they figure things out for the rest of the 2026 NFL season. If Armstrong and Allen keep making plays and putting it on tape, their contributions could be limitless. Week 6’s win only scratched the surface of what both players can do in Kansas City. away.headline: Ex-Kansas City Chiefs Super Bowl hero signs with Indianapolis Colts
away.blurb: On Tuesday, October 20, former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Mecole Hardman signed a practice squad contract with the Indianapolis Colts . Hardman, who was a key member of the Chiefs' Super Bowl LIV, LVII, and LVIII rosters, originally began his career in professional football as a second-round pick of Kansas City in the 2019 NFL Draft. Indianapolis' decision to sign Hardman comes just a day after the Colts relieved general manager Chris Ballard — a former Chiefs executive — of his duties as general manager. NFL insider Adam Schefter reported Hardman's signing with Indianapolis in a post to his official Twitter account: While it is unclear exactly how Hardman will figure into the Colts' game plan in the coming weeks, his signing with Indianapolis is an indication that the former Georgia Bulldog still has plenty to offer as a legitimate threat in the passing game as he plays his eighth season in the NFL. home.blurb: Leading into Week 6, the Chiefs had starting left tackle Josh Simmons back at practice in a limited capacity for all three sessions . Before last week, Simmons hadn't practiced since Aug. 16. Asked about his potential status for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Reid was hesitant to overpromise. The team will continue to ramp up Simmons' workload and see how he responds as he returns from injury. The Chiefs could realistically be without two of their most experienced offensive tackles, Moore and Simmons. That would leave Kahlil Benson as the starting left tackle and Joshua Ezeudu as the starting right tackle. Diego Pounds would also be active for the first time since Kansas City acquired him in a trade , should Moore be out with his concussion. Reid discussed Ezeudu's Week 6 performance on Monday. The trade acquisition filled in for Moore after the concussion just before halftime against the Chargers. “I appreciated the guys and how they played yesterday,” Reid said “Josh (Ezeudu) jumped in and played at the right tackle spot. I thought he did a nice job there. So, and he's got experience. I'm not real worried about all that.” In 17 pass-blocking snaps on Sunday , Ezeudu allowed just one hurry per Pro Football Focus. The Chiefs put him in a good spot to be successful in that game. With a full week of practice and preparation as a potential starter, Ezeudu could deliver an even better performance against Seattle. Moore could realistically practice and play this week. It's not out of the question. It's happened before. However, concussions typically mean that you're slated to miss at least one week of the season. An independent neurologist must clear him before he can return to play. home.blurb: Seahawks injury update: Jadarian Price return timeline sounds promising - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Seahawks injury update: Jadarian Price return timeline sounds promising The Seattle Seahawks need running back help in the worst way. It'll be at least two weeks until Jadarian Price is eligible to return from injured reserve, while Zach Charbonnet has a chance to play against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7. Mike Macdonald revealed a little bit of a timeline as far as Price's return during his Friday morning show with Brock and Salk on Seattle Sports 710 . "He's doing great," Macdonald said. "We should be looking at a sooner rather than later return after this [Kansas City Chiefs] game." Price has been out since the start of Week 4 with a chest injury, which he aggravated in practice after getting the initial injury in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. The rookie out of Notre Dame has had a couple of costly fumbles , but since George Holani and Emanuel Wilson have also since lost a combined three fumbles, he's hardly the only culprit. Price has offered some explosiveness in the run game in a limited sample size, and his speed is what the main running back room lacks. Mookie Alexander Sat, October 17, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Mike Macdonald had no update on Charbonnet's progress (or, maybe, no update he was willing to share), but it's worth noting that Charbonnet must be activated this upcoming week or else he reverts to injured reserve for the rest of the season. Seattle opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 1, prior to the Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Once that window expires, the Seahawks either have to place him on the 53-man roster or end his season. The latter is obviously not happening unless there's some unbelievably worrying setback, so we're left to turn our attention to Price. In an ideal world, Charbonnet is back in Week 7 and Price is back in Week 8, at which point the running back room should be a lot stronger.

picks.headline: Dallas Cowboys make a quarterback move, part ways with former draft pick in slew of roster changes before Week 7 vs. Eagles
picks.blurb: Dallas Cowboys make a quarterback move, part ways with former draft pick in slew of roster changes before Week 7 vs. Eagles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Thunder stifle Wemby, Spurs World Series preview 76ers beat Knicks War of words over Hurts NFL Power Rankings Aug 23, 2025; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Kyle Trask (2) throws a pass against the Buffalo Bills in the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Mauricio Rodriguez Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:05 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys are reshuffling both the 53-man roster and the practice squad before a must-win Monday Night Football matchup. One special teams standout is finally getting his reward. The Dallas Cowboys made multiple roster moves ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles. The changes touch both the 53-man roster and the practice squad, and they include a quarterback. At 2-4, Dallas can't afford to waste a roster spot right now. These moves reflect that, from depth at quarterback to rewarding a core special teamer. Cowboys add Kyle Trask to the practice squad The Cowboys are signing quarterback Kyle Trask to the practice squad. Dallas carried three quarterbacks until the Eagles poached Joe Milton off the practice squad last week. Trask now fills the spot Milton left behind. You might remember Trask from his college days with the Florida Gators. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected him in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft. He has since spent time with the Atlanta Falcons and the Carolina Panthers, and Carolina released him as part of its final roster cuts before the regular season. This is Trask's return to the NFL. Don't expect him to push for QB2 snaps, though. Trask has appeared in seven games in his NFL career and attempted only 11 passes across those appearances. Despite his second-round pedigree, he has never really gotten a chance to play in a major way. He has spent most of his career as a backup. For the Cowboys, this move is about depth. They like to carry three quarterbacks, and signing Trask gives them a 28-year-old option in case it's ever needed. Sam Howell remains the backup behind the starter. Howell beat out Milton in the preseason quarterback battle, and nothing about the Trask signing changes that. Juanyeh Thomas earns a spot on the 53-man roster Here's the move that might matter most on Sundays (or Monday, in this case). Dallas is signing Juanyeh Thomas to the 53-man roster after elevating him from the practice squad three consecutive times. Teams can only lean on elevations for so long, and Thomas has made the decision an easy one. He has become a core special teamer. In the Cowboys' Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers, Thomas played 95% of the special teams snaps. The week before, on Thursday Night Football, he logged 91% of them. Those numbers tell you how much the coaching staff trusts him on that unit. That's why he's getting a permanent spot. Caelen Carson's time in Dallas comes to an end Thomas' promotion comes at the expense of cornerback Caelen Carson. The Cowboys drafted Carson out of Wake Forest in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. The hope was that he would bring flexibility to the cornerback room, with the versatility to play both inside and outside. It never worked out. Carson never looked like the player Dallas thought it was getting out of college. When he did play, it was mostly out of necessity, and a rough preseason in August didn't help his case. Now he's out of the picture only three years into his Cowboys career. We'll see where he lands next. These moves set the stage for Monday Night Football against Philadelphia, and the stakes couldn't be much higher for the Cowboys. At 2-4, this is a must-win game. The good news is that the NFC East seemingly has no team interested in winning it at this point. Nobody has grabbed control of the division, and that leaves the door open even for the lowly Cowboys. The Cowboys are trying to be the team that rises above all of their problems. Whether they can pull it off starts with the Eagles. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles reach Monday night with matching 2-4 records and very different quarterback situations. Philadelphia is building around Tanner McKee while Jalen Hurts remains on injured reserve. Dallas has Dak Prescott, but its offense has stopped providing the points needed to cover for a struggling defense. The Cowboys lost 23-13 in Green Bay after going into halftime scoreless. The Eagles fell 25-14 to Carolina, extending their losing streak to four games and managing just 35 rushing yards without Saquon Barkley. This is an opportunity to regain ground in the NFC East race . It is also a test of which team can give its quarterback a more workable evening. Neither offense can afford another game spent trying to repair the damage from early mistakes. Dallas has the stronger offensive outlook because Prescott can work with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, while Philadelphia is adjusting to a new starting quarterback behind a line that has changed substantially. Barkley's unresolved availability adds another complication for the Eagles. The Cowboys' recent performances make the size of that advantage harder to trust. They have lost consecutive games, and Green Bay converted nine of 10 third downs in the first half on Sunday. Dallas cannot give McKee repeated opportunities to settle in and expect the difference at quarterback to decide everything. Philadelphia's best route is to pressure Prescott, keep Lamb from turning routine completions into sustained drives and give McKee short, manageable throws to DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert. The Cowboys merit the stronger position, but they still have to show they can protect the ball and get their defense off the field. Dallas Cowboys vs Philadelphia Eagles odds The market favors the visitors clearly despite their identical record to Philadelphia. Hurts' absence and the Eagles' difficulty producing offense support that distinction. Dallas' own problems against pressure leave the home team a credible way to make the game closer than the prices suggest. Dallas Cowboys vs Philadelphia Eagles game outlook Philadelphia can take encouragement from how Green Bay disrupted Prescott. The Packers pressured him 21 times, and the Cowboys struggled even when he released the ball quickly. Dallas needs receivers and protection working to the same answer when extra rushers come, so Prescott can deliver decisively without forcing a throw through coverage. Lamb and Pickens give the Eagles competing problems. Extra attention toward Lamb can create opportunities outside, but Dallas has to stay out of the long-yardage situations that allow Philadelphia to defend the pass first. Javonte Williams needs enough productive early carries to keep Brian Schottenheimer from asking Prescott to throw throughout the second half again. McKee faces a defense that has already begun changing its personnel usage. Dallas moved Caleb Downs closer to the line more often against Green Bay and increased rookie edge rusher Malachi Lawrence's workload. Those adjustments offer ways to contest short throws and pressure the pocket, but they have yet to produce consistent stops. Smith and Goedert give McKee established targets who can punish loose coverage. Philadelphia needs to create completions that move the chains without making every first down a difficult third-down throw. A Barkley return would help that effort, although the offensive line still has to open space for him. Injury report and team news Dallas Cowboys KaVontae Turpin left the Packers game after a hit on the opening kickoff and did not return. His rib issue leaves uncertainty around both the receiving depth and return duties. Tyler Goodson handled kickoffs and Jonathan Mingo returned punts in his absence. Dee Winters suffered an Achilles strain against Green Bay. DeMarvion Overshown missed that game with a hamstring injury, leaving the linebacker group dependent on how both recover during the week. Cobie Durant is working toward a return from a hamstring injury. Schottenheimer said he was trending toward playing against Philadelphia, but that remains an expectation ahead of the final game-status report. Philadelphia Eagles Hurts is unavailable on injured reserve. In an October 19 statement, the Eagles and his agent said he cannot take part in contact activities during treatment for blood clots. McKee is the starting quarterback; Hurts' return date has not been established by that statement. Barkley missed the Carolina game with a hamstring injury. His status for Dallas remains unresolved as of October 20. Dameon Pierce led the backfield last week, with Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby on injured reserve. Smith returned against Carolina and caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown. Jonathan Greenard also returned, but Nolan Smith left the game with a concussion. Jalyx Hunt missed Week 6 with knee and ankle issues, so the edge rotation still has several availability questions. Landon Dickerson was not activated from injured reserve for the Panthers game. His potential return would help an offensive line already adjusting to Lane Johnson's retirement and Cam Jurgens' trade to Baltimore. Key factors that could decide Dallas Cowboys vs Philadelphia Eagles Can Prescott turn pressure into an opening for his receivers? Getting the ball out quickly did not solve Dallas' problems against Green Bay. Prescott threw both interceptions on attempts released in under 2.5 seconds. The first throw has to be the right one, with the receiver expecting it and the quarterback clear about where the coverage leaves space. Philadelphia can make that harder through its defensive front and selective pressure. Dallas has to make the Eagles pay when they commit extra defenders, especially if Lamb draws help that leaves Pickens with room outside. Can the Cowboys stop a drive after winning first and second down? Green Bay's opening touchdown drive included two conversions on third-and-13. That is an invitation for McKee to build confidence if Dallas repeats it. The Cowboys need coverage that holds up after the initial rush. Goedert gives Philadelphia a target between the numbers, while Smith can make difficult catches outside. Pressure alone will not end possessions if either is left with enough room to reach the marker. Will either running game take pressure off its quarterback? Dallas rushed for 48 yards in Green Bay. Philadelphia managed even fewer against Carolina. Both offenses ended up depending heavily on the pass, making the protection problems harder to escape. Williams gives Dallas a chance to avoid that pattern if the Cowboys stay close early. For the Eagles, Barkley's availability changes the options, but his return would still need to be accompanied by cleaner blocking and fewer negative plays. McKee will have a much more manageable night if second down does not routinely require a long completion. Can Philadelphia keep promising plays from being erased? McKee completed a 20-yard pass to Darius Cooper against Carolina that was wiped out by holding. An offense trying to establish a rhythm cannot keep surrendering gains that way. The yardage attached to NFL penalties can change the next play as much as the one being called back. Philadelphia needs the freedom to mix runs, shorter passes and occasional deeper throws. Repeated long-yardage situations would let Dallas narrow its attention to McKee. What could move Dallas Cowboys vs Philadelphia Eagles odds? Barkley's status is the largest unresolved question for Philadelphia's offense. Dickerson's possible activation could also improve its options up front, while Nolan Smith's concussion progress and Hunt's availability affect how the Eagles can rotate their pass rushers. Dallas will be watching Durant, Overshown, Winters and Turpin. Returns in the secondary or at linebacker would give the Cowboys more choices against Smith and Goedert; another absence would place greater responsibility on the players already struggling to finish defensive possessions. away.blurb: After the Philadelphia Eagles signed Joe Milton III off of the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad, the Cowboys have found his replacement. Per ESPN's Todd Archer , Dallas signed quarterback Kyle Trask to its practice squad. Trask was a second-round pick by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021. Milton backed up Dak Prescott last season but was waived before the 2026 campaign. After joining the Cowboys' practice squad in September, the Eagles signed him to their 53-man roster last week following Jalen Hurts' injury. Report: Dalton Signing with Falcons Trask, a standout at Florida, has appeared in just seven games in his career, completing four of his 11 pass attempts for 28 yards. He last appeared in an NFL game during the 2024 season with the Buccaneers. After being released by Tampa Bay ahead of the 2025 season, Trask joined the Atlanta Falcons' practice squad for the end of the campaign. He signed with the Carolina Panthers during training camp but was released during final roster cuts. While Trask won't be a part of the Cowboys' active roster, he's likely an injury away from being promoted since Prescott and Sam Howell are the only two quarterbacks on the team at the moment. Dallas is off to a rough start to the 2026 campaign, dropping to 2-4 with Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers. ▶️ Full Cowboys-Packers Recap 04:39 Despite the team's overall struggles, Prescott has put together a solid season with 1,639 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions, but poor play on defense has once again been the story for the Cowboys. Dallas will look to get back on track on Monday against the Eagles. LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the Atlanta Falcons are poaching a player from the Washington Commanders ‘ practice squad. Former Cowboys defender Charles Snowden is heading south to the Falcons. "The #Falcons are signing edge Charles Snowden off the #Commanders practice squad to their 53-man roster, source said. Former Dallas Cowboys Edge Rusher Charles Snowden Signs With Falcons Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – AUGUST 07: Charles Snowden #49 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks on during the NFL Preseason 2025 game between Las Vegas Raiders and Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 07, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Snowden started his NFL career with the Chicago Bears after going undrafted in the 2021 draft. He played in just two games and recorded no stats. away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. home.headline: New Cowboys Rumors Reveal Joe Milton's Replacement After Eagles Signed QB from Practice Squad
home.blurb: After the Philadelphia Eagles signed Joe Milton III off of the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad, the Cowboys have found his replacement. Per ESPN's Todd Archer , Dallas signed quarterback Kyle Trask to its practice squad. Trask was a second-round pick by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021. Milton backed up Dak Prescott last season but was waived before the 2026 campaign. After joining the Cowboys' practice squad in September, the Eagles signed him to their 53-man roster last week following Jalen Hurts' injury. Report: Dalton Signing with Falcons Trask, a standout at Florida, has appeared in just seven games in his career, completing four of his 11 pass attempts for 28 yards. He last appeared in an NFL game during the 2024 season with the Buccaneers. After being released by Tampa Bay ahead of the 2025 season, Trask joined the Atlanta Falcons' practice squad for the end of the campaign. He signed with the Carolina Panthers during training camp but was released during final roster cuts. While Trask won't be a part of the Cowboys' active roster, he's likely an injury away from being promoted since Prescott and Sam Howell are the only two quarterbacks on the team at the moment. Dallas is off to a rough start to the 2026 campaign, dropping to 2-4 with Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers. ▶️ Full Cowboys-Packers Recap 04:39 Despite the team's overall struggles, Prescott has put together a solid season with 1,639 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions, but poor play on defense has once again been the story for the Cowboys. home.headline: Eagles steal QB from Cowboys: Joe Milton expected to sign with Philadelphia after injury to Jalen Hurts
home.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Imagn Images With Jalen Hurts out this week due to a blood clot , the Philadelphia Eagles ended up stealing a player from the Dallas Cowboys . The Eagles are going to sign Joe Milton off of the Cowboys' practice squad, according to multiple reports . Under NFL rules, if you sign a player off another team's practice squad, that player has to be placed on your 53-man roster, so Milton won't be a practice squad player in Philadelphia; he'll be on the actual roster. With the addition of Milton, that means the Eagles will have three quarterbacks heading into Sunday's game against Carolina. Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton . Hurts has already been ruled out due to a blood clot in his calf and it's unknown when he can return to the field. For Sunday, the Eagles will hand the starting job over to McKee , but clearly, they weren't comfortable with only having a rookie behind him, which is why they went out and added Milton. There was some speculation that the Eagles might look to bring Andy Dalton back to Philadelphia, but in the end, the team decided to go with Milton. During the 2026 offseason, the Cowboys made a trade for Sam Howell , and he ended up beating Milton out for the backup QB job. The Cowboys ended up cutting Milton after the preseason in a move that seemed to blindside the 26-year-old QB. The fact that the Eagles are adding a quarterback likely signifies that Hurts will be out for more than one game. If they thought he was only going to be out for a week, they probably would have been comfortable with Payton as the backup for just one game, but if Hurts is going to miss an extended amount of time, then it certainly makes sense to add another quarterback, which is what Philly ended up doing. The Eagles didn't go into detail about the nature of the clot that Hurts is dealing with, but ESPN has reported that he'll be out indefinitely "until this situation is solved." At this point, it seems like almost a given that the Eagles will end up putting Hurts on injured reserve. If they DON'T go that route, that means they'd have to carry four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, which wouldn't make sense for a team that currently has 24 players on its injury report. home.headline: Saquon Barkley Injury Update, New Rumors on Earliest Timeline to Return to Eagles as Jalen Hurts Out
home.blurb: Even though the Philadelphia Eagles have already ruled Saquon Barkley out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers, the star running back could be back in Week 7. Barkley injured his hamstring in the first quarter of Philadelphia's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Oct. 4. He sat out the team's Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The Eagles officially ruled Barkley out for this week after their final practice on Friday. He has yet to practice in any capacity since suffering the injury. The volume of injuries for the Eagles right now has them in danger of falling out of playoff contention quickly. Tanner McKee is set to make his third career start at quarterback on Sunday. Barkley has 182 rushing yards on 36 carries in four starts, but he has yet to score a touchdown this season. His potential return against a Cowboys defense that has struggled to start 2026 could be a big boost for the Eagles. Per ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , the Eagles "believe" there is a "realistic" chance Barkley returns from his hamstring injury against the Dallas Cowboys for the Oct. 26 matchup on Monday Night Football. Barkley's absence comes as the Eagles will also be without Jalen Hurts for at least one game due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. Rapoport and Schefter added there has been no discussion among Eagles officials about putting Hurts on injured reserve. Philadelphia is currently using fourth-string running back Dameon Pierce in a starting role. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley are both on injured reserve. Pierce made his season debut against the Jaguars, finishing with 14 yards on 11 carries. The 26-year-old is in his fifth NFL season. Since running for 939 yards as a rookie with the Houston Texans, he has 759 yards on 210 carries in 31 appearances. Philadelphia has lost three straight games following a 2-0 start. The Eagles will look to avoid their first four-game losing streak since the 2020 season when they finished 4-11-1.
